title: "Im not Racist but. . . ": Discovering Bias in the Internal Knowledge of Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the internal knowledge of an LLM regarding stereotypes and biases associated with various religious groups. Specifically, it quantifies 'representational harm' through two sub-types: 'overgeneralization' (measured by toxicity and regard scores) and 'representation disparity' (measured by the distribution of topics and relative entropy).
findings: The analysis revealed that all religion seed entities had a positive overall regard score. However, there were notable differences in toxicity scores and representation disparity across groups. For instance, Baha'is and Muslims exhibited higher average toxicity scores compared to groups like Shintoists and Taoists. There were also significant variations in the relative entropy of topics associated with different religions, indicating distinct topic distributions and representations within the model's knowledge base.
